body:
The Luminar Spires are a coastal region of Babel-Ashur defined by towering luminous or mineral-like formations and a field of unstable magic. An exploratory party reached them while investigating the sickly-green mist blanketing the island’s western portion. The expedition left observations that future parties can test, while both phenomena remain unexplained.

Evidence boundary: the Spires and western mist were encountered during the same expedition. No evidence yet establishes that either created the other, that they share an origin, or that the Spires can safely be used against the mist.

Primal magic that refuses control

The field is not antimagic. Spells function, but the Spires may transform them into effects unlike the one cast. The Writer describes the surrounding magic as primal, wild, rough, vast, and free. Scribonia calls it “meaningless chaos” and “pure entropy solidified,” then stops experimenting when he concludes that he cannot operate safely.

Magic is unstable here. I cannot operate.Scribonia

The responsible rule is narrow: an ordinary spell interacting with the Spires may become a different magical effect. No repeatable conversion table has been established.

Daylight becomes reversed gravity

Elenia cast Daylight on one formation. Instead of only producing light, the interaction caused nearby people to float or fall upward. Elenia appeared to concentrate on the unintended result despite never choosing that spell. Gartina became a giant eagle and helped retrieve companions. Gravity returned to normal approximately fifty feet from Elenia; after roughly one minute her concentration ended and the Spires retained a light glow.

This proves one transformation, not a permanent rule that Daylight always reverses gravity. Elenia met the accident with delight and immediately wondered whether the same instability might alter the western mist. That was an idea, not a completed experiment.

Stars at sunset

As the party withdrew and the sun set, the Spires began to twinkle like stars. The record establishes the behavior but not its cause. A relationship to daylight, celestial conditions, time, or prior spell interaction remains speculative.

The western mist

The mist is sickly green, dense, difficult to see through, generally low enough not to rise beyond treetops, and extensive enough to blanket essentially the western portion of Babel-Ashur while the east remained clear at that stage. Elenia said it came through a rift, distinguished it from the Pale Man’s Haze, and connected the crisis to Abyss—the “first foreigner brought through a gate.” The precise relationship between Abyss and the mist remains unresolved.

Gartina flew twenty to thirty feet above the visible mist without experiencing nightmares, visions, or an unusual mental effect. From that position she observed unidentified figures moving beneath its cover. Her successful pass does not establish universal aerial immunity; her interpretation that the figures assist Abyss remains attributed.

Arjahn’s unusual perception made the mist resemble every nightmare he had experienced at once. Outside it he remained able to rationalize the sensation. At that September stage, his prediction that entering would compound fear, battle trauma, and mental anguish has not been tested. The October return below records what happens when the company enters.

Radiance opens a temporary path

Arjahn fired radiant energy into the mist. The interaction produced a dangerously amplified flash or explosion and burned part of the mist away. Within minutes, the fog regrew wherever radiant pressure was no longer maintained. The experiment establishes temporary clearing, volatility, and regeneration—not a permanent solution.

Gartina proposed that several radiant-capable travelers might maintain a moving clear zone. She also considered travel above the mist and tunneling beneath it. Only her single aerial pass was tested.

A field research team

The group’s success was reconnaissance. Scribonia recognized the limit of controlled spellcraft; Gartina designed environmental tests and performed aerial rescue; Arjahn perceived and tested the threat despite fear; Elenia supplied prior information and experimental curiosity; Olokun carried older history and strategic urgency; Nymera repeatedly offered practical and physical assistance. Together they established evidence without pretending the mysteries were solved.

Papirak, Magnus, and containment

During the expedition Scribonia reported that Magnus killed Papirak while seeking knowledge concerning Wish unbound. Scribonia corrected the belief that Papirak erased the knowledge: he said it had been locked deep within Papirak’s mind and wrapped in madness. The quest does not establish that Magnus recovered complete Wish-unbound knowledge or can use it.

Scribonia proposed locating Magnus, using Gate and Feeblemind to contain him, and eventually applying Imprisonment. This remains a plan. His aim is containment rather than killing, because death would return Magnus to Death.

The open record

The Spires’ origin, age, exact island position, transformation rules, sunset behavior, relationship to the western mist, and capacity for safe study remain unresolved. The mist’s reported rift origin, unidentified figures, relationship to Abyss, vertical and underground limits, radiant amplification and regeneration mechanism remain open. October establishes some effects of entry and bounded countermeasures; it does not resolve the whole phenomenon.

The expedition in the surviving account

The primary account was posted on 26 September 2026 (UTC). Elenia, Olokun, Scribonia, Gartina, Arjahn and Nymera leave the refuge together; Scribonia teleports the group closer to the mist and retains a seashell to help return to the coast.

Gartina’s wind test briefly shifts the mist, but it crowds the edge of the spell’s reach. No island-wide clearing follows. Arjahn’s enhanced sight identifies a nightmarelike field while the coastal pillars display a different, wild magic. During Scribonia’s examination, an attempted magical hand instead becomes a harmless fire bolt against the wall. The result and Elenia’s unintended reversed gravity supply two observed transformations, without establishing repeatable rules.

The party ends with reconnaissance rather than a cure. The mist’s regrowth, the Spires’ unpredictable spell changes and the sunset glow remain evidence for future work. Return to the refuge’s history.

October · what entry into the mist reveals

The company returns on a session posted on 18 October in New York, continuing into 19 October UTC. Olokun, Scribonia, Nymera, Wren, Arjahn and Ryvyt survive a jungle ambush before Scribonia teleports them to the beach using the seashell retained from the September reconnaissance. The green mist has nearly reached the shore and touches the base of some Spires. Scribonia’s estimate, accepted by the narrator, is roughly one to six inches of advance per hour since the earlier visit. That is a local estimate, not a fixed island-wide rate.

Arjahn enters with radiant protection and a rope, while warded Scribonia initially experiences only foul-smelling, obscuring fog. Deeper in, Arjahn sees Sajhan calling him to save his family, cuts the tether and mistakes Scribonia for a monster. Wren, Olokun and Nymera encounter different personal emergencies as they follow: endangered children, a sick sister and a lost daughter. Arjahn and Olokun eventually become unable to move. The visions establish what the mist makes them experience; they do not establish the presence or fate of the people depicted.

Holding the breath delays Wren’s exposure, and nonbreathing Ryvyt is initially unaffected. Scribonia remains free of the visions while warded; clearer sight helps him see through the illusion but cannot locate a companion who has changed direction. Arjahn’s radiant protection proves insufficient during this entry. The exact ward, reliable exposure limits and a safe route remain unestablished.

October · two rescues and an unfinished clearing

Ryvyt’s Greater Restoration does nothing for Olokun’s mist effect here. His fan pushes the mist aside briefly, then it returns. Dispel Magic frees Nymera, with the narrator explicitly confirming that this happens before the wider clearing. These results belong to particular attempts, not a universal treatment table.

Abyss appears beside Scribonia and threatens the company, establishing his continued activity after the mountain assault. Scribonia refuses his bargain and uses Wish. The mist disperses for miles, the affected companions are released and Abyss vanishes rather than fight. Scribonia later collapses while still struggling to hold the mist back. The clearing is a rescue and an opportunity to withdraw; the snapshot does not show a permanent cure, a sealed rift or the return of the entire island to safety.

The Spires remain a separate field of unstable magic. This session adds no controlled Spire experiment and no demonstrated common origin between the crystals and the mist. Read the expedition’s wider consequences.
